果树和茶树、桑树种下后一直留在地里，只在结果季收获，天数从结果季第一天算起。日净: Fruit trees, tea plants and mulberry trees stay in the field after planting and are harvested only in their fruiting season; days count from the first day of that season. Net per day subtracts the sapling price; later fruiting seasons need no new sapling, and "without the sapling" shows the net per day then. A grown fruit tree bears 1 fruit a day, up to 3, and is shaken once full; tea plants and mulberry trees need 2 more days after each harvest. Each mulberry harvest gives 2 Mulberry Leaves and 2 Mulberry Fruits, and the fruit is sold raw when the leaves are processed. In the first spring there's no time to plant early, so trees are planted at the start of the month and harvested once grown. Banana, cacao and mango trees grow only in the greenhouse and bear fruit all year, so they're listed every season. Fruit trees need two empty squares between them, so each takes more than 1 square.
